A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MedAgentGym and Med-Copilot. Their complete main texts and appendices are readable, and shared datasets, methods, tables, and figures can be matched despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original model benchmarking, SFT/DPO experiments, scaling and ablation studies, external evaluations, and an 83-task human study.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical results and adds PPO/GRPO experiments, further external evaluations, code-quality measurements, and a trajectory-validity audit.

M1.justification: V1 trains agents through SFT, DPO, and verifier-guided self-improvement. V2 adds online PPO and GRPO with environment interaction and correctness plus code-format rewards (Section 5.1). These extend the training procedure; the underlying execution environment, agent scaffold, and verifier remain.

E1.justification: V2 adds BixBench for external biological data-analysis evaluation and a fully preprocessed MIMIC-Extract scenario that reduces data-preparation requirements (Appendix F.7). These extend evaluation within existing biomedical coding coverage; the original twelve-source benchmark remains.

E2.justification: V2 adds codex-mini to Table 3 and HuatuoGPT-o1-7B and Qwen2.5-Coder-14B-Instruct to the external comparison in Table 5. PPO/GRPO training alternatives are also compared. V1's DPO-without-SFT 7B external row disappears, although its internal ablation remains in v2 Table 10.

E3.justification: V2 introduces online-RL experimental settings, five additional code-quality/efficiency metrics, a raw-versus-fully-preprocessed MIMIC-Extract comparison, and an audit sampling over 250 trajectories. Existing benchmark splits, interaction limits, temperatures, and SFT/DPO settings are retained, with several disclosures moved to Appendix E.

E4.justification: New analyses examine code complexity and maintainability, preprocessing difficulty, domain-specific coding errors, and whether successful trajectories contain logically flawed solutions (Appendices F.1, F.6–F.8). Existing backbone scaling, debugging, toolset, and internal SFT warm-up analyses remain; their relocation does not constitute new evidence.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without training-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new trajectory-audit percentage is an additional descriptive result, not a change in uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: V2 adds PPO/GRPO results: GRPO averages are 62.17/71.42 internally and 36.63/47.02 externally for 7B/14B models. Earlier SFT+DPO internal scores of 59.90/66.37 remain under the DPO labels. New results also cover codex-mini, BixBench, processed MIMIC-Extract, code quality, and the audit reporting less than 1% flawed-code successes. The external DPO-only 7B average of 21.31 is removed.

T1.justification: The execution-verification formulation, positive/negative trajectory definitions, POMDP framing, and verifier probability formula remain substantively unchanged. V2 adds no theoretical propositions, proofs, or formal derivations.

C1.justification: V1 emphasizes SFT and continued DPO training as routes toward proprietary-model performance. V2 makes demonstrated offline and online RL central contributions and explicitly claims gpt-4o-comparable performance on both in-distribution and out-of-distribution tasks. This extends the central claim beyond the earlier training demonstration.

C2.justification: V1 describes limited, inconsistent external generalization and proposes stronger optimization as future work. V2 interprets GRPO as improving transfer and attributes substantial MIMIC-Extract difficulty to preprocessing requirements. It also adds modality limitations, resource-related inequity and representation-bias concerns, and interpretations of code quality and domain-specific correctness.

D1.justification: Appendix E adds VeRL/Docker integration and PPO/GRPO settings: batch size 128, learning rate 1e-5, rollout temperature 0.6, and KL coefficient 0.001. V2 also specifies additional artifact contents and verifier release, and discloses human-study IRB approval and unpaid participation. Existing prompts, SFT/DPO details, and dataset-access information largely persist.

R1.justification: V2 updates the literature with works including Biomni, STELLA, Paper2Agent, BixBench, and HybridFlow, while dropping DeepResearchGym. Its main related-work discussion emphasizes biomedical data-science workflows and agentic RL. Much of v1's review survives in Appendix B, preserving the central positioning against narrative medical reasoning and evaluation-only benchmarks.

P1.justification: V2 retitles the paper, extensively rewrites the introduction and main related work, compresses the benchmark discussion, and reorganizes substantial material into appendices. It adds standalone ethics and reproducibility statements and expands limitations and broader impacts. These are extensive narrative and structural revisions.

P2.justification: V2 adds environment and RL schematics, code-quality and external-difficulty tables, and three domain-specific case-study figures. It changes the opening radar chart to domain-based axes, redraws and relocates diversity displays, separates former Figure 6's panels, and redistributes training results between main and appendix tables. Typography and page layout also change substantially.

improvement.justification: V2 tests PPO/GRPO, proposed as future directions in v1, and adds useful transfer, preprocessing, and solution-validity evidence. However, some new interpretations overreach their supporting material: Table 8 shows mixed efficiency changes, and Figure 17 labels a function using an undefined age_val variable as correct. The expanded evidence improves the paper, but these reporting weaknesses limit the net quality gain.
